This is stored XSS from external feed content.

judged_text: TopicEmbed.import stores third-party RSS/article HTML as the post's raw content with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations: true, bypassing Discourse's sanitizer, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked. Any hostile or compromised feed/embedded source can inject arbitrary script into the post content; it renders inside the embed iframe (and the topic page), giving stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `app/models/post.rb`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`), and the embed UI renders the result with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). Since imported RSS/article HTML (`contents`) can contain hostile markup (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers) and nothing in this diff sanitizes it before storing/rendering, this introduces a stored XSS risk on the Discourse origin (at least within the embed iframe, and potentially anywhere the post is displayed using `cooked`).
